    AI Overview

    AI Mode replied:

    The sky is blue because Earth's atmosphere scatters the shorter, smaller waves of blue sunlight in all directions more than it does the longer-wavelength colors. 
    How It Works
    • White Light: Sunlight appears white, but it is actually made up of all the colors of the rainbow combined. 
    • Different Wavelengths: Each color travels in waves of different lengths. Red and yellow light have long waves, while blue and violet light have short, choppy waves. 
    • Rayleigh Scattering: When sunlight reaches Earth, it collides with gases in the atmosphere (mostly nitrogen and oxygen). Because blue light has a shorter wavelength, it bounces off these gas molecules and spreads across the sky much more easily than other colors
